intro.title: useKeyPress
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple interactive Angular component that detects and responds to keyboard key presses. You will learn how to use Angular's event binding to listen for keyboard events like 'keydown' and 'keyup' in the template. The main technologies involved are TypeScript for logic and Angular's template syntax for handling events. By the end, you'll have a component that displays a message when a specific key, such as 'Enter' or 'Escape', is pressed, helping you understand event-driven interactions in Angular applications.
intro.usecase: The useKeyPress pattern is essential for creating keyboard-accessible interfaces in real-world Angular applications. Developers implement this in admin dashboards where users navigate data tables with arrow keys, in forms where pressing Enter submits data, and in interactive tools like design editors where shortcuts (Ctrl+S to save) improve workflow efficiency. This pattern also powers accessibility features in modals that close with Escape, search filters that respond to keyboard input, and navigation menus that support keyboard-only users. Mastering useKeyPress enables you to build professional applications that meet both user experience expectations and accessibility standards.
